title: APPENDIX: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY

Bill Gardner presented the symbol of the old, new and eternal law: an olive branch—symbol of peace according to the law, its omission meaning "peace, no war, between you and me"; the turkey feather on the end of the arrow meaning "friendship, morality and brotherly love," he said. The gift was accepted by President McMahon and ordered deposited in a place of safe keeping as a sacred relic.

Martha Buford May read an original poem, titled, "The Second Reunion."

Lee A. Clark submitted a report from the Board of Managers covering draft of a Constitution and By-Laws, based upon a tentative set drafted in 1938, with additional regulations for the guidance of the Association. The report of the Board was adopted.

President McMahon delivered the following address:

"Your president has served for this first year in office. Before the president relates what went on he had the good fortune to be privileged to work with, and to the assistant of a great statesman and patriot. Your association is to be congratulated for having one who has and is yet serving the U. S. Government with skill and faithfulness, as its president.

"The life of this organization began in fact two years ago, and it will be a pleasure to report some of the activities of the first year of our life as it is to be hoped that with the ending of the launching year ends all period of doubt and uncertainty, and the Association swings into its mature stride.

"The provisions of the new Constitution and By-Laws have my hearty approval. They are good; they have been, first, advocated and, afterward, paid by every hours as were destroyed by others—whose constructive work on them justifies their present day drive.

"My official family has by hard work made a success of launching our Association, and I recommend that each of them be returned to office for the ensuing year.
